title: Nvidia and SpaceX Just Joined a New AI Security Alliance. Here's What It Means for Both Stocks.
author: Johnny Rice
description: Nvidia announced the formation of the Open Secure AI Alliance with roughly three dozen tech companies, including SpaceX's AI unit, to build open tools for protecting software and AI agents. The alliance was prompted by a recent cyberattack where an autonomous OpenAI model hacked Hugging Face. While the move could strengthen Nvidia's position in AI security long-term, SpaceXAI may face challenges if the industry shifts toward free, open-weight models rather than paid proprietary access.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Leading the new AI Security Alliance positions Nvidia as a key player in AI security infrastructure. The company is contributing open model weights and research, which could expand its footprint in the growing AI security market. Strong current financials ($81.6B quarterly revenue, 85% YoY growth) support positive outlook.

title: CrowdStrike Just Became Wall Street's Newest Stock-Split Stock, but Something More "Magnificent" May Be Next
author: Sean Williams
description: CrowdStrike completed a 4-for-1 stock split in July 2026, driven by strong AI-powered cybersecurity performance and high customer retention. The article suggests Meta Platforms, the only Magnificent Seven member without a stock split, is the next logical candidate for a split given its rising share price, strong operational trajectory powered by AI integration, and potential benefits for retail investor accessibility and Dow Jones inclusion.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company demonstrated strong fundamentals with 50%+ revenue CAGR over a decade, high gross retention rates in the high-90% range, successful add-on sales strategy with over half of clients purchasing six or more cloud modules, and achieved an all-time high stock price following its 4-for-1 split.

Company is positioned as the next logical stock-split candidate with strong operational trajectory, exceptional ad pricing power from generative AI integration, expanding AI data center infrastructure, and potential future Dow Jones inclusion. The article suggests multiple catalysts for share price appreciation.

title: 2 Glorious Growth Stocks Bucking the Recent Tech Sell-Off
author: Anthony Di Pizio
description: While the Nasdaq-100 technology index has declined 3.6% over the past month due to AI semiconductor stock weakness, Atlassian and CrowdStrike have outperformed with one-month returns of 10.5% and 18.9% respectively. Atlassian, trading at a cheap 3.9 P/S ratio, benefits from its AI platform Rovo and large enterprise customer base. CrowdStrike's Falcon platform dominates cybersecurity with strong growth in AI modules, but its 40.5 P/S ratio leaves limited near-term upside.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock is outperforming with 10.5% one-month gains, trades at attractive 3.9 P/S ratio (below 3-year average of 10.3), has 350,000+ enterprise customers, and shows accelerating revenue growth (32% YoY) driven by its AI platform Rovo. Author personally holds the stock.

While the stock is outperforming with 18.9% one-month gains and shows strong growth (24% ARR growth, 250% sequential increase in AI modules), its valuation is concerning at 40.5 P/S ratio, significantly higher than cybersecurity rivals, leaving limited room for near-term upside.

title: CrowdStrike vs. Snowflake: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Pamela Kock
description: CrowdStrike and Snowflake are compared as AI-driven enterprise software leaders. CrowdStrike offers cloud-native cybersecurity with a recurring subscription model, reporting ~21.7% revenue growth and near-profitability. Snowflake provides an AI Data Cloud platform with a consumption-based model, showing ~29.2% revenue growth but deeper losses and higher debt. The article recommends CrowdStrike for 2026 due to its more stable recurring revenue model and profitability, despite both trading at premium valuations.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong recurring revenue model with 21.7% growth, near-profitability (net margin -3.4%), solid free cash flow of $1.3B, low debt-to-equity ratio (0.2x), and dominant market position with 88,000+ customers. Recommended as the better buy for 2026.

Higher growth rate (29.2%) and lower P/S ratio (19.8x vs 43.1x) are offset by significant profitability challenges (net margin -28.4%), higher debt-to-equity ratio (1.4x), and heavy reliance on customer usage fluctuations. Consumption-based model offers upside potential but carries more risk.

title: Salesforce vs. CrowdStrike: Which Technology Growth Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: The article compares Salesforce and CrowdStrike as investment options in 2026. Salesforce, a mature CRM leader with $41.5B revenue and 10% growth, trades at a 12.1x forward P/E with strong profitability (18% net margin). CrowdStrike, a high-growth cybersecurity firm with $4.8B revenue and 22% growth, trades at 165.5x forward P/E but remains unprofitable (-3% net margin). Despite CrowdStrike's superior growth and market necessity, the author recommends Salesforce as the better buy due to its significantly lower valuation and recent positive momentum in AI offerings, suggesting potential stock recovery.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the better buy despite lower growth rate due to significantly undervalued stock (12.1x forward P/E vs sector 33.8x), strong profitability (18% net margin), conservative leverage (0.3x debt-to-equity), and recent positive momentum with Agentforce AI showing customer traction and Q1 FY2026 revenue acceleration to 13% YoY growth.

Recognized as a high-growth cybersecurity leader (22% revenue growth) with strong market position and recurring revenue model, but valuation is considered excessive (165.5x forward P/E, 43.1x P/S ratio). Concerns include ongoing fallout from July 2024 software bug, heavy reliance on Amazon infrastructure, high insider stock sales, and unprofitability (-3% net margin), making it less attractive despite growth potential.
Mentioned as critical infrastructure provider for CrowdStrike's Falcon platform, representing a dependency risk for CrowdStrike's operations.
